packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-03 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (working notes appended face by face; summary at end)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files of packet-03 (a directory listing of the packet showed the filename packet.json, which I did not open).

=== image-001.jpg (overview, label "A") with tiles image-002.jpg, image-003.jpg ===

Layout (observation): a tall narrow parchment strip, about 6 cm wide by 15 cm high against the ruler, upright. Almost the whole surface is blank or abraded and carries two vertical rows of sewing/stitch holes plus horizontal slits; it looks like a binding strip (tentative). Writing survives only as a sliver about 0.5-0.8 cm wide down the right-hand edge: the beginnings of some 20+ lines of a small dark Gothic book hand, i.e. the left edge of a text column whose remainder is cut away. Red is visible at three points in that sliver: a red stroke (paraph or initial fragment?) about one third down, another small red mark, and a red rounded initial or paraph (D-like or C-like bowl) about two thirds down. No running title, no gloss visible.

image-002.jpg (upper right edge), only line-beginnings of 1-3 letters each, very faint:
image-002 l.1: [large or doubled letter, heavier ink, P? or ff?] + 1-2 minims
image-002 l.2: [illegible, 2 strokes]
image-002 l.3: ?insti / ?nisti [4-5 minim-letters, heavier]
image-002 l.4-8: [illegible traces of line beginnings]
image-002 l.9 (below a horizontal tear): [illegible]; a capital-like A? shape lower down
image-002 l.10-15: [illegible traces]
image-002 bottom: red oblique stroke (paraph?) at left of the sliver

image-003.jpg (lower right edge; overlaps the bottom of image-002 at the red stroke):
image-003 l.1: [illegible]
image-003 l.2: red stroke (same as bottom of image-002)
image-003 l.3: [illegible]
image-003 l.4: ?pmi / ?pnisi [p + minims, heavier ink]
image-003 l.5: ?p(er) / pd [p with stroke]
image-003 l.6: [illegible]
image-003 l.7: ?mo / ?nio
image-003 l.8-9: [illegible]
image-003 l.10: red rounded initial or paraph (bowl open to the right, D/C-like) with a red horizontal stroke
image-003 l.11-13: [illegible traces]
image-003 l.14: ?tr / ?ti [dark traces at the bottom]

No connected text is recoverable from this face: every line is cut after one to four letters.

=== image-004.jpg (overview, label "A", other face of the same strip) with tiles image-005.jpg, image-006.jpg ===

Layout (observation): the same strip turned over; the written sliver is now at the left edge and shows the ENDS of about 20 lines (right edge of a column cut away on its left). Same small Gothic book hand, black-brown ink; a horizontal crease/tear crosses after about line 7. No red seen on this face. The tiles are only about 185 px wide, so each line yields 2-5 letters.

image-005.jpg (upper left edge), line ends:
image-005 l.1: [illegible traces] ?q̃ m / ?gñ
image-005 l.2: [trace with abbreviation hook, ?9 (-us) or ?p]
image-005 l.3: ]?n ho / ]o ho[ (edge torn after "ho")
image-005 l.4: ]?uir / ]?mir
image-005 l.5: ]?nilla / ]?milia  (ends in -illa or -ilia; ?-nulla)
image-005 l.6: ]?ce ē / ]ic(e) e(st)?  (final letter with macron)
image-005 l.7: ]?est / ]?eff  (at the horizontal tear)
image-005 l.8: [illegible, on the crease]
image-005 l.9: ]?ibus / ]?thag  (word with ascender and a suspension stroke; damaged)
image-005 l.10: ]?mois / ]?inoib(us)?  (minims + "ois" with a mark above: possibly -o(n)is / -(n)ib(us))
image-005 l.11: ]gra / ]g(rati)a?  (g + superscript mark + a)
image-005 l.12: ] .d.n.  (three letters set off by points: ". d . n ." - an abbreviation by initials, read with fair confidence)
image-005 l.13: ]?sp(eci)ale / ]?ffiale / ]?spūale  (long-s or f + "iale"/"uale" with abbreviation mark)
image-005 l.14: ]?anr / ]?āni  (cut at tile bottom)

image-006.jpg (lower left edge; its first lines repeat image-005 l.12-14, not additional text):
image-006 l.1: ] .d.n.  (= image-005 l.12)
image-006 l.2: ]?sp(eci)ale / ]?ffiale  (= image-005 l.13)
image-006 l.3: ]?ānr / ]?aur / ]āni
image-006 l.4: ] ad  (with a stroke beneath or a following abbreviation: "ad" or "aď"; fairly clear)
image-006 l.5: ]?ctur / ]?atur / ]?uir  (ends "-tur" or "-uir")
image-006 l.6: ]?b / ]?l[illegible] (one ascender at the cut edge, rest faded)
image-006 l.7-8: [illegible, abraded]
image-006 l.9: ]?nilia / ]?filia / ]?alia  (ascender + "ilia"/"alia", faint)
image-006 l.10: ]?eo. / ]?en.  (ends with a point)
image-006 l.11: ]?es / ]?is  (faint, with a descender)
image-006 l.12: ]?an. / ]?am.  (ends with a point)
image-006 l.13: [short dark horizontal stroke only]

No connected text is recoverable from this face either: only 2-5 letters at each line end.

=== image-007.jpg (overview, label "B") with tiles image-008.jpg, image-009.jpg ===

Layout (observation): a second strip, about 6 cm wide by 16.5 cm high, upright, same kind of object (two vertical rows of stitch holes, horizontal slits, mostly blank/abraded surface; faint offset or erased traces at the far left including a circular mark). A written sliver about 1 cm wide runs down the right edge: line BEGINNINGS of some 28-30 lines of the same small Gothic book hand. One marginal letter stands in the left margin beside a line about two thirds down (a bold "F"-like sign or "ff"/paraph, black), and the line it marks is underlined; a faint red mark sits a few lines above it and another tiny red fleck at the right edge near line 7. Two text blocks seem separated by a slightly larger gap before the marked line (tentative).

image-008.jpg (upper right edge), line beginnings:
image-008 l.1: τc. qd[  ("etc." sign + "q" with superscript d/o: ?q(uo)d / ?q(ua)d[ )
image-008 l.2: uj. p. l?[  /  iij. pl[   (a numeral-like group ending in j, a point, then "p" + ascender: looks like a citation by number)
image-008 l.3: ep(iscop)e? / epe. x[  ("epe" with abbreviation stroke, point, then x or "v")
image-008 l.4: ?p(er) uir[ / ?pp iur[  (p with stroke through descender + minims; a hole/white fleck on the first letters)
image-008 l.5: ?p(ro) uid[ / [illegible] (on the horizontal tear, tops lost)
image-008 l.6: no(n) e[  /  no 6[
image-008 l.7: ?hanc . / ?hoiu(m) .  (h + 3-4 letters, then a point; red fleck at edge)
image-008 l.8: ?nuss(us) i[ / ?uiso i[  (minims + long-s or l, then a tall letter with stroke)
image-008 l.9: ?b(e)n(e)fi[ / ?s(ed) hab[  (first letter with abbreviation mark, then h/b-ascender)
image-008 l.10: ?fratis / ?stans / ?fiano  (long-s or f + "tan"/"ran" + s/o)
image-008 l.11: ?Trinita[ / ?Promia[ / ?quoma[  (enlarged first letter, then "ma"/"nita")
image-008 l.12: en. p(ro)[ / ?eni p(ri)[
image-008 l.13: ?sibi . c[ / ?Sili. ε[
image-008 l.14: ?qu(od) [illegible] / ?l. si a[  (smudged)
image-008 l.15: ?cu(m) o[ / ?τ(et) o[  (first sign with a bar above, then "o")
image-008 l.16: in p(er)[ / in p(ro)[  (clear "in p" with abbreviated p)
image-008 l.17: nit(ur)? so[ / nis fo[  ("ni" + superscript sign, then long-s/f + o)
image-008 l.18: sic uu[ / fit uu[ / ficuu[  (long-s/f + "ic"/"it" + minims)
image-008 bottom: small red mark at the edge

image-009.jpg (lower right edge; its first three lines repeat image-008 l.16-18, not additional text):
image-009 l.1: in p(er)[  (= image-008 l.16)
image-009 l.2: nit' so[ / nis fo[  (= image-008 l.17)
image-009 l.3: sic uu[ / ficuu[  (= image-008 l.18)
image-009 l.4: [illegible; blank or abraded]
image-009 l.5: [red mark, then] ?si[ / ?li[  (faint)
image-009 l.6: [blank or abraded - possible gap between text blocks]
image-009 l.7: ?q(uo)d uo[ / ?Ex po[ / ?τc po[  (first sign heavy and smudged, with a mark above; then "po"/"uo")
image-009 l.8: MARGIN: bold F (or ff / paraph-like sign).  TEXT, underlined: sp(irit)ual[  ("spūal" with abbreviation stroke, preceded by a short stroke that may be "i" or part of the margin sign: ?ispūal / ?in spūal[ibus?]). The underline runs under this word.
image-009 l.9: ?ce p(re)sb[ / ?te p̄si[ / ?cc. ff[   (2 letters, then p with stroke + long-s)
image-009 l.10: uico. [ / ?nicoi[ / ?meo.[  (minims + "co", then points)
image-009 l.11: leg(is)? . s[ / leg(um) . s[  ("leg" with superscript abbreviation, point, then s or "8")
image-009 l.12: ?n. c. p[ / ?q. e. q[  (short abbreviated groups separated by points, faint: looks like another reference by sigla)
image-009 l.13: ?i. l. c[ / ?p(er) leo[  (faint)
image-009 l.14: ?de ce[ / ?τc ce[
image-009 l.15: ann?i[ / ?āni i[ / ?anim[  (with a horizontal stroke above; a dark line/tear runs through)
image-009 l.16: ut(ri)? d[ / ?iu(ri)s di[ / ?ui(r) do[  (minims with superscript sign, then "d" + letter)
image-009 l.17: ?p(ro) qo[ / ?h' is[  (faint, descender at left)
image-009 l.18: ?etiia[ / ?emo[ / ?enua[  (faint; hole at right)

Observation on content of this face (not an identification): the point-separated short groups and numeral at image-008 l.1-3 and image-009 l.11-13 look like abbreviated references/citations rather than running prose, and the underlined word with a marginal letter at image-009 l.8 looks like a lemma or heading opening. All of this is tentative because only 3-6 letters per line survive.

=== image-010.jpg (overview, label "B", other face of strip B) with tiles image-011.jpg, image-012.jpg ===

Layout (observation): strip B turned over; written sliver about 1 cm wide at the left edge = line ENDS of about 30 lines (right edge of a column). Same hand. Faint show-through or offset of further writing is visible near the right edge of the strip (upper right and middle right), too faint to read in the overview and not covered by a tile. No red seen on this face except one possible tiny red tick in image-012 l.5. A horizontal slit crosses after line 5 and another near line 26.

image-011.jpg (upper left edge), line ends:
image-011 l.1: ] no(n) in / ] no. m   ("no" with stroke, point/hole, then minims)
image-011 l.2: ]p(ro)uilia / ]p(ri)uilia / ]puilia   ("p" + "uilia"/"uilui" with a final stroke above: possibly p(ri)uil(eg)ia - uncertain)
image-011 l.3: ]honore.   (clear; "h" first letter slightly cut; ends with a point)
image-011 l.4: ] g(ra)? p(re)l / ] g̃ p̃s   ("g" with superscript mark, a hole, then "p" with stroke + tall letter)
image-011 l.5: ]?l. s(ecundu)m / [illegible] (on the horizontal slit; only tops/bottoms)
image-011 l.6: ]entia(rum)? / ]encia3 / ]nicia3   (ends "-cia"/"-tia" + a 3-shaped sign = -rum / -m / -que?)
image-011 l.7: ] . d' 9 dt. / ].d(e) (con)d(i)t.   (point, "d" with hook, the 9-shaped con- sign, "d" + "t"/"i" with point: reads like an abbreviated reference, e.g. "d(e) (con)d..." - uncertain)
image-011 l.8: ]ys an / ]us an(te)? / ]y(m)o an   ("ys"/"us" then "an" with a stroke above)
image-011 l.9: ]c habui / ]thalui / ]chatui   (ascender group + "aui"/"abui" with final stroke above)
image-011 l.10: ]. al' as / ]calas / ].a.l'.af   (faint first part; "al" with abbreviation, then "as"/"af")
image-011 l.11: ]?e hy / ]?thy / [illegible]   (faint)
image-011 l.12: ]? fi eai / ]?sicut / ]?ficai   (long-s/f + i/c + 3 letters)
image-011 l.13: ]?ij me / ]?y me / ]?h(ab)ent   (faint)
image-011 l.14: ]?ati / ]?igi / ]?iai   (faint, with stroke above)
image-011 l.15: ]?inat. / ]?nnut. / ]?mat.   (faint; ends with a point)
image-011 l.16: ] sicut / ] fuert / ] sunt   (long-s + minims + t; "sicut" or "suat"?)
image-011 l.17: ] s(ed) sup(er)? / ] t(ibi) sit / ] ß sup   (sign with stroke above, then long-s + "up"/"it" with abbreviation)
image-011 l.18: [illegible, abraded]
image-011 l.19: [illegible, abraded]
image-011 l.20: ]?. e. p. s. / ]?τ. f. s.   (short letters separated by points, faint; cut at tile bottom)

image-012.jpg (lower left edge; its first two lines repeat image-011 l.16-17, not additional text):
image-012 l.1: ] sicut / ] sunt   (= image-011 l.16)
image-012 l.2: ] s(ed) sup(er)? / ] ß sit   (= image-011 l.17)
image-012 l.3: [illegible, abraded]
image-012 l.4: ]?. e. p. s. / ]?τ.f.s.   (= image-011 l.20; point-separated letters)
image-012 l.5: ]?mu(n) τ / ]?nu(m) i / ]?hui(us) τ   (minims with stroke above, then a Tironian-et-like or "i"/"T" sign, possibly touched in red)
image-012 l.6: ]?l(ite)ras / ]?tene / ]?l[c]eua   ("l" or "t" + "eu"/"en" + "a"/"s" with a small stroke above)
image-012 l.7: ]?no. q(uod) / ]?mo. q̃ / ]?uio. q(ui)   (minims + o, point, "q" with abbreviation)
image-012 l.8: ]?q(uam) in / ]?g. m / ]?igitur   (faint; descender then minims)
image-012 l.9: ]?t(ur) iste. / ]? e(ss)e. / ]?c. iste.   (a superscript sign, then "iste"/"esse" followed by a point)
image-012 l.10: ]?enser / ]?ener(e) / ]?eu(er)sus   ("en" + long-s + "er"/"et" with abbreviation stroke: ?-enset / ?-ensis et)
image-012 l.11: ]p(er) me / ]p(ro) me / ]h(ic) me   (descender letter with stroke, then "me" with a macron above: m(e)e / me(n)?)
image-012 l.12: ]a. g(ra)ue. / ]a. g(rat)ie. / ]a. g̃ne.   ("a" + point, then g with superscript abbreviation + "ue"/"ne"/"ie", ending with a point)
image-012 l.13: ]c τ ser / ]t (et) ser / ]e i sec   (clear Tironian et between; "ser"/"sec"/"fer" at the cut)
image-012 l.14: ]?uio q(ue) / ]?tiio q(uod) / ]?ioo. q̃   (on a horizontal slit)
image-012 l.15: ] sp(irit)u s(anct)i? / ] sp(e)ci / ] ip(s)o si   (long-s + p with stroke above + "o"/"u" + "si"/"sti": ?spōsi = sponsi / ?sp(irit)us)
image-012 l.16: ]?inaio. / ]?rmaio. / ]?uuato.   (minims + "aio"/"ato", ending with a point; ?-in(ati)o / ?-rmatio)
image-012 l.17: ]t(ur) . τ p(ro) / ]c(ur) . r p(er)   (superscript sign, point, then "τ"/"r" + "p" with descender stroke: ?(et) p(ro) / ?r(esponsio) / ?rp')
image-012 l.18: ]?e. τ j / ]?. r j   (faint; edge torn)
image-012 l.19: ]?t / [illegible]   (torn foot)

No connected text is recoverable from this face: 3-7 letters at each line end. The clearest readings are "honore." (image-011 l.3), "in"/"no(n)" (l.1), the "d' 9..." reference-like group (l.7), "τ ser" (image-012 l.13), "me" (image-012 l.11).

=== image-013.jpg (overview, label "C") with tile image-014.jpg ===

Layout (observation): a third strip, horizontal, about 14.5 cm wide by 3.7 cm high. It preserves the UPPER MARGIN of a page and the first two (and the tops of a third) lines of TWO COLUMNS: the left column ends at about 7.5 cm, an intercolumnar space of about 1.3 cm follows, and the right column runs to the torn right edge. In the upper margin, centred over the page (above the intercolumn), stands a RED sign: a capital "L" with a small "2"-shaped/9-shaped sign above right (tentatively a running title such as a book letter/number - "L" + superscript, perhaps L(iber) with a numeral; I do not interpret further). A vertical ruled line and prickings/holes at the far left; a vertical slit at upper right. The script is the same small Gothic book hand, upright. The left part of the left column and all of the right column are very faint (abraded); only the right half of the left column is dark.

image-014.jpg (tile of the written lower band):
